decisions.reason: The approved FAQ content still describes Big Block prizes, tickets, $6,000 payouts, and a two-block prize system, all of which become obsolete when Big Blocks are removed.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Marcus, please remove the big blocks and redirect that extra $8 to me. The new breakdown should be:
$30 purchase, $12 to me, $10 to the affiliate, and $8 to the block prize pool.

That should improve my bottom line without materially affecting sales, while also making the game mechanics and marketing simpler.

An even arrangement between me and each community member, together with an equal opportunity to win the continuing $900 prizes, feels consistent with the project's ethos.

Explain one-time-email-code or SIWE access, automatic $10 referral commissions, Small Block prize-ticket assignment, winner notifications, automatic $900 wallet payouts, fund-export guidance, and the confirmation email containing the mint number, NFT details, and dashboard link.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the Big Block ticket lifecycle and narrows the contexts to Small Block tickets.
Removing Big Blocks does not change the automatic wallet-transfer behavior for winners of the continuing Small Block prizes.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records the $12 founder share, $10 affiliate commission, $8 prize-pool share, and Small-Block-only destination.
The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete Big Block ticket-counter attribute.
The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the Big Block tickets issued for coded referral mints while preserving Small Block ticket issuance.
The $10 no-referral commission and random-recipient selection remain valid and are independent of whether a Big Block draw exists.
The candidate state contains no Big-Block-specific ticket attribute or scope; allocating one ticket to a random existing NFT remains valid for the continuing prize system.
The source changes the primary-purchase allocation and removes Big Blocks but does not cancel the established rule that secondary royalties fund the remaining prize pool without creating tickets.
Active and expired ticket transfer semantics remain valid for the continuing Small Block tickets, and the candidate state contains no Big-Block-specific transfer attribute.
